title: Staged experiment acceptance criteria and escalation ladder for model routing
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Context: We need a prescriptive, repeatable acceptance and escalation framework for model-routing experiments (A/B and canary) across hosted and dedicated deployments. Goal: reduce time-to-decision for rollouts, ensure safe quality/latency trade-offs, and provide clear operator actions when gates fail. This ticket captures the acceptance criteria, measurement windows, signal thresholds, automated gating logic, and a human escalation ladder for the engineering, SRE, and PM orgs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All experiment routes must have a minimum instrumentation set (traces, per-route token breakdowns, user-facing error counts) before traffic is diverted; 2) For canaries, P50 and P95 latency vs baseline and error rate regressions are measured over a minimum 60-minute steady window; 3) Quality regressions (semantic score on seeded prompts) must be below 2% absolute degradation vs baseline or the experiment is blocked; 4) Automated rollback triggers defined and tested in staging; 5) Dashboards and alerts (pager and Slack) created and verified; 6) Playbook steps documented and acknowledged by on-call SRE and PM
milestones: M1 (2026-03-03): Draft acceptance thresholds and instrumentation checklist; M2 (2026-03-10): Implement dashboards and automated rollback triggers in staging; M3 (2026-03-20): Dry-run with synthetic traffic and chaos scenarios; M4 (2026-03-25): Small-scale canary (1% traffic) and evaluate metrics; M5 (2026-03-30): Ramp to 10% or rollback based on gates; M6 (2026-04-01): Post-mortem and documentation update
evaluation_metrics: Performance: latency P50/P95 (ms), tail latency spike count, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec. Reliability: 5xx rate, request success rate, KV cache hit ratio. Quality: seeded semantic similarity score, rouge/bleu where applicable, human eval sample pass rate. Business: conversion lift or feature-specific engagement delta. Safety: hallucination rate on safety prompts. Thresholds: P95 < baseline+30ms; 5xx delta < 0.05%; semantic score delta > -2% blocks rollout; business uplift evaluated after 24h at >=10% traffic
instrumentation: Required events: request-id, route-id, model-version, prompt-hash, token-counts, backend-latency-breakdown, KV-cache-hits. Dashboards: per-route latency/error heatmaps, model comparison table, seeded-prompt quality timeline. Alerts: severity-1 pager if 5xx delta > 0.2% or semantic score regression > 5% in 30m; severity-2 Slack for P95 > baseline+60ms for 30m. Tracing: end-to-end traces linked to request-id. Data retention: 14 days for raw traces, 90 days for aggregated metrics.
rollout_plan: Stage A (staging validation): run synthetic traffic and verify automated rollback works; Stage B (canary 1%): 1% traffic for 60m steady window; Stage C (canary 10%): 10% traffic for 24h with periodic manual checks; Stage D (ramp to 50%+): conditional on business metrics and no gate violations for 48h. Each stage requires sign-off by PM + on-call SRE. Feature flag gating uses 'model-routing.v2' toggle with percentage controls and instant kill switch
escalation_ladder: Level 1 (automated): system triggers rollback and notifies #canary-alerts channel; Level 2 (on-call SRE): page rotation (primary) and confirm rollback state, add mitigation; Level 3 (engineering lead): investigate root cause, triage hotfix or partial rollback; Level 4 (PM + Eng Director): business impact assessment and customer communication plan. Contacts: On-call SRE rotation (docs link), Eng lead: Priya Nair, PM owner: Liam Chen, Escalation channel: #redwood-ops
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: latent quality regressions not captured by seeded prompts. Mitigation: include human blind eval sample of 200 examples during canary. Risk: backend resource exhaustion under burst traffic. Mitigation: circuit-breaker on routing layer and autoscaling threshold. Risk: alert fatigue from noisy thresholds. Mitigation: tune alert windows and introduce composite signals before paging.
monitoring_playbook: If automated gate fails: 1) Confirm rollback executed; 2) Acknowledge incident in channel, attach dashboard snapshot; 3) Capture request-id examples and seed-set failures; 4) Triage with model owner and SRE; 5) Decide restore criteria (hotfix vs re-run experiment). If latency degrades without errors: 1) Inspect KV cache hit ratio and batching logs; 2) Check underlying infra scaling events; 3) Coordinate with infra team for temporary capacity bump
